goal: Introduce the protected control-plane tier and the digest-covered control_plane grant that expresses it, so a specialized workflow-authority task can be authorized to maintain runtime-policy files while an ordinary task still cannot reach them by adding a path to allowed_paths. Rules only: this task grants nothing and changes no runtime behaviour.
non_goals: Carrying a control_plane grant of its own — this task introduces the mechanism and must not exercise it
Any runtime enforcement: no hook, no permissions rule, no sandbox, no producer agent
Moving .agent/roles.json, .agent/tasks/**, .claude/settings.local.json or .git/** out of the absolute floor
Editing .agent/tasks/README.md, which is inside the Tier 0 floor
Re-sealing any existing contract, or changing any existing contract's digest
Widening the canonical meaning of r4, or altering the risk or production_effect taxonomies
Mutating the live GitHub ruleset, branch protection, or any repository setting
Merging anything, or making any production, database or store change
acceptance_criteria: A protected control-plane tier is defined as a closed registry of paths, disjoint from the absolute floor, and every entry obeys the existing decidable path grammar — exact paths or dir/** subtrees only, never a filename wildcard

A contract may express authority over a protected path only through a dedicated control_plane field carrying a grant and its protected paths; the same authority expressed through ordinary allowed_paths is rejected
The grant vocabulary is closed and each grant maps to its own subset of protected paths, so a grant cannot authorize a protected path outside its mapping and no grant authorizes the tier as a whole
A contract carrying control_plane must declare owner_role workflow-authority and risk of at least r3; any other role is rejected, and the canonical meaning of r4 is unchanged
No absolute-floor path may appear in control_plane, in allowed_paths, or in any grant mapping

Optional binding fields are a stated schema-evolution rule rather than a special case: a required binding field is always covered by the digest, an optional one is covered if and only if the key is present, and the rule is expressed generally so a future optional binding field inherits it
Adding the field leaves every existing sealed contract byte-identical, proven by a spec that recomputes the digest of each contract currently in .agent/tasks and asserts it is unchanged
A present control_plane affects the digest, and changing, widening or removing it changes the digest again

Mechanical review treats the effective implementation scope as allowed_paths united with the granted protected paths, so a validly granted protected path is in scope and an ungranted one is still reported out of scope
Mechanical review keeps the absolute floor unconditionally blocking and keeps the self-edit check on the contract's own file independently blocking, neither of which any grant can satisfy

Malformed, unknown or internally inconsistent control_plane declarations are rejected rather than partially honoured, including an unknown grant, a non-array path list, a path outside the tier, a path that fails the grammar, and a grant/path mismatch

docs/AUTOMATION-AUTHORITY.md documents the three tiers, the grant, the digest rule and what a grant still cannot do; .agent/tasks/README.md is deliberately left unchanged because it is inside the floor
stop_conditions: Introducing the field would change any existing contract's digest — stop rather than re-sealing, because .agent/tasks/** is on the floor and no contract may authorize that write
The tier or the grant cannot be expressed within the existing decidable path grammar — report before widening the grammar, which would weaken containment reasoning everywhere
The change turns out to require editing .agent/roles.json, .claude/settings.json or .agent/tasks/README.md — stop and report the governance conflict
Runtime enforcement turns out to be necessary to make the model coherent — stop, because that is a separate task with its own review
The work turns out not to fit workflow-authority / r3 / none — report before implementing
notes: PR A of the runtime-enforcement sequence, rules only. It follows a cold-start probe which established that project-subagent frontmatter PreToolUse hooks do not execute in this managed runtime (Claude Code 2.1.252): zero hook events, zero registration, every path escape succeeded, the producer overwrote its own guard, and the deny-all control still allowed the write. The one primitive that did hold is subagent tools/disallowedTools allowlisting, which is platform-enforced. Settings-level enforcement is therefore the only remaining route, and .claude/settings.json sits on the absolute floor — hence this tier. Classification: workflow-authority because it is control-plane governance; r3 because tools/verify-task-contracts.mjs and tools/review-protocol.mjs are CI/workflow authority and the risk model already places control-plane authority at r3, with r4 reserved for direct production authority; production_effect none because no runtime behaviour changes and merging deploys nothing. This contract deliberately carries no control_plane grant: the task that introduces a mechanism must not be the first to exercise it.
